# Runbook

What to do when an NvSnap alert fires, and how to follow one capture or
restore from start to end. The alerts are in
`deploy/helm/nvsnap/files/prometheus-rules.yaml`; the series they read are
described in [METRICS.md](METRICS.md). Every alert is at severity `info`.

The commands assume the chart's defaults: the agents and the capture
records are in `nvsnap-system`.

## Following one capture or restore

Everything below takes `kubectl` alone.

1. **Which capture a pod belongs to.** A GPU pod NvSnap captured or
   restored carries the capture record's key and, restored, when:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n <ns> get pod <pod> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.nvsnap\.io/criu-group}{"\n"}{.metadata.annotations.nvsnap\.io/criu-restored}{"\n"}'
   ```

   A pod with neither started cold: `nvsnap.io/fallback-reason` says why,
   when the webhook decided it.

2. **What happened to it, in order.** The agents record events on the
   instance's first rank (`NvsnapCaptured`, `NvsnapCaptureFailed`,
   `NvsnapCaptureRefused`, `NvsnapRestored`, `NvsnapRestoreFailed`), on
   every GPU pod (`NvsnapStarted`, with its time to Ready from creation
   and from scheduling), and on a restored rank killed during teardown
   (`NvsnapTeardownDeadline`):

   ```bash
   kubectl -n <ns> get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep Nvsnap
   ```

3. **The capture record.** Its state, the agent release that captured it,
   its members and nodes, its last 10 restores (`restores`, as
   `RFC3339=seconds`), and why it failed (`reason`):

   ```bash
   kubectl -n nvsnap-system get cm nvsnap-criu-group-<key> -o yaml
   kubectl get nvsnapfunctions -o wide       # every function version: state, method, last restore
   ```

4. **The agents' summary lines.** One per capture, restore and pod start,
   on the agent of the node it ran on (the restore's on the agent that
   drove it, the first rank's):

   ```bash
   kubectl -n nvsnap-system get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/component=agent -o wide   # the agent of each node
   kubectl -n nvsnap-system logs <agent> | grep -E 'nvsnap (capture|restore|pod ready) summary' | grep <key-or-pod>
   ```

   A restore's line has `outcome`, `reason`, `error` and `seconds`; its
   ranks' lines (`criu`, `gpu`, `rank` phases) are on their own nodes'
   agents. A rank's teardown logs `group teardown:` lines with
   `teardownSeconds`.

5. **The function version's history.** Its last 50 restores, with their
   restore, scale-up and teardown times, outlive the pods:

   ```bash
   kubectl get nvsnapfunctions                               # RESTORES, GONE, P50-SCALEUP-S, P50-TEARDOWN-S
   kubectl get nvsnapfunction <function-version-id> -o jsonpath='{range .status.history[*]}{.at} {.outcome} restore={.restoreSeconds} scaleup={.scaleUpSeconds} teardown={.teardown}/{.teardownSeconds}{"\n"}{end}'
   ```

6. **Where the time went, across many.** The dashboard
   (`deploy/helm/nvsnap/files/grafana-dashboard-nvsnap-history.json`) has
   scale-up, restore phases, teardown and the cached captures per cluster.

## NvsnapAgentMetricsMissing

No agent has been scraped for 15 minutes, so no other NvSnap alert can
fire.

- Are the agents running? `kubectl -n nvsnap-system get ds nvsnap-agent`
- Is the ServiceMonitor there, where the cluster's Prometheus reads it?
  `kubectl get servicemonitor -A | grep nvsnap-agent`, then compare its
  namespace and labels with the Prometheus's `serviceMonitorSelector` and
  `serviceMonitorNamespaceSelector` ([METRICS.md](METRICS.md#install)).
- Can Prometheus reach an agent? Its targets page (`/targets`, or
  `/api/v1/targets?state=active` filtered on `job="nvsnap-agent"`) shows
  each agent target's last scrape and its error. A target with an error
  but an agent that serves metrics is a network path or a NetworkPolicy
  between Prometheus and the agents.
- Does an agent serve metrics? Its `/metrics` is on port 8081. This goes
  through the API server, so it does not show that Prometheus can reach it:
  `kubectl -n nvsnap-system port-forward <agent> 8081`, and once it prints
  `Forwarding from`, in another shell
  `curl -s localhost:8081/metrics | grep nvsnap_build_info`.

## NvsnapAgentDown

One agent has not been scraped for 15 minutes. While it is down, its
node's pods are neither captured nor restored, and a restored instance's
teardown on that node is not driven: its pods go at the end of their grace
period.

- `kubectl -n nvsnap-system get pod <pod> -o wide` and
  `kubectl -n nvsnap-system describe pod <pod>`: crash-looping, evicted, or
  its node not ready?
- `kubectl -n nvsnap-system logs <pod> --previous` for the last crash.

## NvsnapWebhookErrors

The admission webhook the agents serve answers with errors. It fails
open: the pods it errors on are admitted unchanged and start cold.

- The errors by status: the dashboard's "Webhook answers by status", or
  `sum by (code) (rate(nvsnap_webhook_requests_total[10m]))`.
- The agents' webhook log lines: `kubectl -n nvsnap-system logs <agent> | grep subsys=webhook | grep -i error`.

## NvsnapAdmissionMissed

Ranks of a captured instance started without the webhook mutating them
(reason `not-admitted`: the API server could not reach the webhook and its
failure policy let the pod in; `opted-out`: the pod carries
`nvsnap.io/inject=false`). Such an instance is not captured while those
ranks run.

- The ranks: `kubectl get events -A --field-selector reason=NvsnapNotAdmitted`
- `not-admitted`: check the webhook's reachability (NvsnapWebhookErrors,
  the agents' readiness) and the API server's
  `apiserver_admission_webhook_fail_open_count` for `rootfs-restore.nvsnap.io`.

## NvsnapRestoreFailed

A restore ran and failed; its pods are replaced and start again. Its
`reason` label is the class of the failure (`criu`, `gpushare`, `timeout`,
`rdma`, `mptcp`, `fetch`, `other`, [METRICS.md](METRICS.md#metrics)).

- The restore: `kubectl get events -A --field-selector reason=NvsnapRestoreFailed`,
  then [follow it](#following-one-capture-or-restore). The event's
  message has the error.
- A capture that keeps failing to restore is given up after its third
  failure (state `restore-failed`) and the next instance captures anew;
  restores on GPUs the probe found faulty (`gpu-fault`) are not counted
  against it ([design](../design/GPU-FAULT-PROBE.md)).
- `gpushare` failures are the GPU checkpoint library's
  ([design](../design/GPUSHARE.md)): keep the agent's log lines of the
  restore and the rank's container log for the library's owners.

## NvsnapRestoreNotRunRepeatedly

Restores could not run, three times or more in 30 minutes: the checkpoint
could not be fetched to a node (`fetch`), or the instance's placeholders
never all ran. Each try replaces the pods.

- `fetch`: the dashboard's "Checkpoint fetch to a node" shows which source
  fails; the restoring agent's summary line has the error.
- Placeholders: are the instance's pods pending (no GPUs free, a node
  cordoned)? `kubectl -n <ns> get pods -o wide`.

## NvsnapTeardownKilled

A deleted restored rank was killed at the end of its grace period before
every rank of its restore had exited ([design](../design/GROUP-TEARDOWN.md)).
The ranks still running lose their peer, and their GPUs can stay held
until the driver recovers them (minutes).

- The rank: `kubectl get events -A --field-selector reason=NvsnapTeardownDeadline`.
- Which rank did not exit: the ranks' `nvsnap.io/criu-teardown-exited`
  annotations (set when a rank's workload is gone), and the agents'
  `group teardown:` lines on the instance's nodes.
- A rank whose agent was down from before the delete is not driven; its
  peers wait for it to the end of their grace period.

## NvsnapCaptureFailed

A capture `failed`, its pods never started under the GPU library
(`gpushare-failed`), or it restored but its pods never served
(`unverified`). The configuration's next deployment captures again, up to
three times.

- The capture: `kubectl get events -A --field-selector reason=NvsnapCaptureFailed`,
  then [follow it](#following-one-capture-or-restore). The record's
  `reason` has the error.
- Captures that failed for the workload's own doing (`reason`
  `workload_exited`: it ended during the capture; `no_gpu_process`: it had
  nothing on the GPU) do not fire this alert; they are on the dashboard's
  "Capture outcomes".

## NvsnapInventoryStale

No agent exports the inventory of capture records, or its scans have
failed for 10 minutes. Only the cached-capture panels are affected.

- The leader: `kubectl -n nvsnap-system get lease nvsnap-capture-inventory -o jsonpath='{.spec.holderIdentity}{"\n"}'`
  (a node name), and its agent's log:
  `kubectl -n nvsnap-system logs <agent> | grep 'capture inventory'`.
- No Lease, or one held by a node with no agent: the agents' RBAC must let
  them get, create and update Leases in the capture records' namespace
  (`nvsnap-system` by default; `templates/agent-rbac.yaml`, checked by
  `TestAgentRBACCoversTheInventoryLease`).

## NvsnapCaptureStuckVerifying

A capture has been verifying for over 3 hours while its namespace still
exists. A capture is verified when the pods of a restore of it have served
for 6 minutes; until then only its own namespace restores from it.

- The record: `kubectl -n nvsnap-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.data.state=="verifying" and (.data.abandonedAt|not)) | "\(.metadata.name) \(.data.startedAt) \(.data.sourceNamespace)"'`
- Its namespace's pods: deleted and restored again and again within 6
  minutes (a test that cycles its instance) never verify it. Otherwise
  [follow its last restore](#following-one-capture-or-restore).
